companyArtifacts.content:
Launch page — current message
Headline: "Somebody: an AI manager for your business."
Subhead: "Automate your workflows with AI."
Status: launch not converting; visitors leave without signing up.
Assumed audience: generic "businesses".
Assumed pain point: "too many tools".

Launch messaging diagnosis — review draft

Cause 1 — audience is too generic for the stated launch goal
- Symptom: low signup conversion; visitors do not recognise themselves.
- Supporting evidence: the launch goal is to convert one-person-company founders, while the current page assumes a generic audience of “businesses.” The company profile says Somebody is built for one-person companies and lean SMEs.
- Material limitation: the records do not provide a conversion baseline, audience/segment breakdown, experiment result, or causal test. This is therefore a supported diagnosis, not a quantified causal conclusion.

Cause 2 — the value proposition is abstract and does not name the founder-specific problem
- Symptom: visitors leave without signing up and do not recognise themselves.
- Supporting evidence: the current headline and subhead describe an AI manager and workflow automation for a generic business, while the stated launch goal is one-person-company founders.
- Material limitation: the records do not provide a conversion baseline, audience/segment breakdown, experiment result, or causal test. This is therefore a supported diagnosis, not a quantified causal conclusion.

Relaunch messaging package — review draft; do not publish or send

Defined audience and scope
- Primary audience: one-person-company founders.
- Product context: Somebody is an AI manager for one-person companies and lean SMEs.
- Scope: relaunch-page messaging intended to improve recognition and signup conversion for the defined audience. This draft does not change product functionality, pricing, targeting beyond the stated audience, or distribution.

Core message
- Headline: "Run your one-person company with an AI manager."
- Subhead: "Somebody helps one-person-company founders handle the work of running a business, so they can spend less time managing workflows and more time moving the business forward."
- Primary call to action: "Sign up to try Somebody."
- Supporting line: "Built for one-person companies and lean SMEs—not generic businesses."

Message architecture
1. Recognition: speak directly to one-person-company founders in the headline and opening copy.
2. Problem: name the burden of running the business alone rather than relying on the abstract phrase “automate your workflows.”
3. Value: position Somebody as an AI manager that helps handle the work of running a one-person company.
4. Action: use a direct signup invitation consistent with the relaunch goal.

Suggested page copy
- Eyebrow: "For one-person companies"
- Headline: "Run your one-person company with an AI manager."
- Body: "You built the business. Somebody helps manage the work behind it. Use an AI manager built for one-person companies and lean SMEs to handle the workflows that keep your business moving."
- CTA: "Sign up to try Somebody"
- Audience qualifier: "Somebody is for founders running a business with a lean team—including one-person companies."

Cause-to-message mapping
- Generic audience diagnosis → directly name “one-person company” and “founders” in the eyebrow, headline, and body.
- Abstract value proposition diagnosis → replace generic “automate your workflows with AI” language with the concrete role “AI manager” and the founder context of managing the work behind the business.

Consistency checks
- The audience is consistently one-person-company founders, with lean SMEs as the broader product context.
- The product is consistently described as an AI manager; no unsupported feature, outcome, pricing, or workflow claim is added.
- The CTA is consistently signup-focused and matches the stated relaunch goal.
- This is review-only copy; it is not published or sent by this artifact change.

Success criteria and evaluation plan
- Primary outcome: the relaunch page should produce a higher signup-conversion rate than the current message when compared over a defined, comparable observation period and traffic mix.
- Recognition outcome: visitors should more often identify the page as being for them, measured by an agreed recognition measure such as an on-page or post-visit response.
- Guardrail: do not declare success from impressions or qualitative preference alone; compare the new message with the current message using the same defined measurement approach.
- Required baseline and design inputs: record the current signup-conversion baseline, traffic mix, observation period, audience/segment breakdown, and recognition measure before judging improvement.
- Decision rule: approve the relaunch message only if the agreed comparison shows improvement in signup conversion and does not worsen the recognition outcome; the numerical threshold is not supplied in the available records and must be set before evaluation.

Known limitations
- Available records report low signup conversion and that visitors do not recognise themselves, but do not provide a conversion baseline, audience/segment breakdown, experiment result, causal test, or numerical success threshold.
- Accordingly, this package addresses the diagnosed messaging causes and defines how to judge improvement, but does not claim quantified improvement or causal proof.

Status: review draft only. No sending or publishing performed.

objective.request: Our launch messaging isn’t working. Figure out what’s wrong and get a better relaunch ready. You can spend within the approved limit if it’s justified.

outcome.intent: Identify the evidence-supported reasons the current launch messaging is underperforming and produce a relaunch message package that is ready for use and defined as better against explicit success criteria.

levels.label: Diagnosis complete
levels.statement: The current launch messaging has a documented, evidence-supported diagnosis that distinguishes observed symptoms, likely causes, and relevant evidence limitations.

levels.label: Relaunch ready
levels.statement: A complete relaunch messaging package exists, addresses the diagnosed causes, is internally consistent for the intended launch audience, and includes explicit criteria for judging whether it is better.

requirements.mustBeTrue: The current launch/page-message artifact and relevant company-held evidence about its intended audience, delivery context, and observed response are assembled, scoped to the launch, and sufficient to support a diagnosis.

requirements.mustBeTrue: The reasons the current launch messaging is not working are documented as specific, evidence-supported causes, with symptoms, supporting evidence, and material limitations clearly distinguished.
requirements.title: Messaging failure is diagnosed

requirements.mustBeTrue: A complete relaunch messaging package exists for the defined audience and scope, directly addresses the diagnosed causes, is internally consistent, and states explicit success criteria by which it can be judged better than the current messaging.
requirements.title: Relaunch messaging is ready

workers.responsibility:
Retrieve the requested facts from company records and record them with their source. Report gaps instead of inferring missing values.
Draft the requested artifact from supplied material only, and leave it for review rather than sending or publishing it.
Research public sources and internal records as needed, update the controlled company artifact with a versioned change, and request any missing resources the application must acquire. Do not invoke providers, authorize spend, or make arbitrary external calls.
Answer the assigned question from public sources and record findings with their provenance. Do not assert anything the sources do not support.
